cover letter
Bachelors degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training
Minimum 8 years years of relevant experience.

Applies advanced professional concepts and the University of California Washington Center's (UCDC) organizational objectives to resolve complex issues creatively and effectively in support of its academic programs, residential services, and administrative operations. Works with campuses and financial contacts to understand financial commitments, billing, and fund management. Collaborates with internal and external stakeholders at all levels to coordinate solutions across UCDC's academic, residential, and administrative functions.

20% Financial and resource planning: Gathers, analyzes, and summarizes financial and resource information to develop recommendations for UCDC’s annual budgets, operating forecasts, and long-term resource plans. Works with UC campuses and financial contacts to clarify financial commitments, anticipate funding requirements, and inform resource allocation.
This is a two-year contract appointment. This position is located in Washington, DC.

20% Complex budget and financial project support: Provides analytical support for complex budget, financial, and resource projects in collaboration with UCDC leadership, UC campuses, and financial contacts. Evaluates funding sources, expenditures, and resource needs and recommends approaches to support programmatic and operational priorities.

20% Auxiliary services financial analysis, invoicing, and billing: Works with UCDC auxiliary services to coordinate invoicing and billing for parking, guest housing, and conference planning activities. Analyzes related revenues and expenses, verifies billing information, and works with UC campuses and financial contacts to research discrepancies and coordinate payment resolution.

15% Leadership reporting and process improvement: Prepares financial reports, forecasts, and data analyses to support leadership decisions on resource allocation and long-term planning. Develops recommendations for internal policies and procedures to improve financial reporting, fund management, and auxiliary-service invoicing and billing.

15% Budget development and resource allocation: Coordinates the collection and review of budgetary and resource requirements during the annual budget process and other planning activities. Works with UCDC auxiliary services, UC campuses, and financial contacts to align anticipated revenues, financial commitments, and resource requests with operational needs.

10% Campus and financial liaison: Serves as a liaison among UCDC, UC campuses, financial contacts, and internal and external constituents on financial commitments, billing, and fund management. Coordinates information sharing and follow-up to clarify funding responsibilities and resolve financial questions related to parking, guest housing, conference planning, and resource allocation.
Ability to identify, collect, and analyze information from multiple sources.
Advanced knowledge of finance policies, practices, and systems.
Advanced ability to effectively present complex finance related information both verbally and in writing in a clear and concise manner.

Advanced interpersonal skills at all levels within the organization; advanced service orientation and critical thinking skills; and attention to detail. In depth ability to use organizational skills to multi-task in a high volume environment.
In depth ability to use multiple spreadsheet and database software tools to gather information for specialized, complex financial analysis, fiscal management, and financial reports.
Ability to adapt to changing priorities.
Ability to function as a member of a team.
Advanced knowledge and understanding of internal control practices and their impact on protecting University resources.
